t:
(a) 
Public Law 89–188 is amended under heading “Inside the United States” in section 101, as follows:

        (1) 
Under the subheading “continental army command, less army materiel command (First Army)”, with respect to “Fort Devens, Massachusetts”, strike out “$11,008,000” and insert in place thereof “$11,964,000”.
 
        (2) Under the subheading “army materiel command”, with respect to “Jefferson Proving Ground, Indiana”, strike out “$52,000” and insert in place thereof “$71,000”.
 
        (3) 
Under the subheading “army materiel command”, with respect to “Sharpe Army Depot, California”, strike out “$175,000” and insert in place thereof “$261,000”.
  
    (b) 
Public Law 89–188 is amended by striking out in clause (1) of section 602, “$252,661,000” and “$309,522,000”, and inserting “$253,722,000” and “$310,583,000”, respectively.

fable.w: This section only amends dollar amounts authorized for military construction at specified Army installations in Public Law 89-188. There is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government; the only tempting hook is the procedural amendment language, which is purely fiscal.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of amendments to appropriation amounts for specific military installations. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. The text merely adjusts funding levels within the federal budget.
qwen_block.s: Public Law 89–188 is amended under heading “Inside the United States” in section 101, as follows: (1) Under the subheading “continental army command, less army materiel command (First Army)”, with respect to “Fort Devens, Massachusetts”, strike out “$11,008,000” and insert in place thereof “$11,964,000”.

opus.w: The section only changes funding amounts for Army construction projects at named installations and the total authorization limits in section 602 of Public Law 89–188. No party outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any federal decision. The amendment wording ("strike out ... insert") is ordinary drafting language, not a participation process.
opus.b: This section only changes dollar amounts for military construction projects under Public Law 89–188. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. The only plausible trap is the procedural phrasing ("is amended," "strike out ... insert"), but that is just drafting language for an amendment. Nobody outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends specific dollar amounts in a previous Public Law regarding military appropriations. It does not establish any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from parties outside the federal government. The text is purely a legislative adjustment of funding levels.
qwen_chat.s: Under the subheading “continental army command, less army materiel command (First Army)”, with respect to “Fort Devens, Massachusetts”, strike out “$11,008,000” and insert in place thereof “$11,964,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing appropriation amounts involves some form of consultation or decision-making process. However, the text itself is purely a mechanical amendment of dollar figures in a previous law. It does not describe any process of consulting with outside parties, holding hearings, or forming advisory committees. It is a legislative directive on funding levels, not a procedural requirement for participation.
